transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. Can you start by telling me what brings you in today?

Well, the main thing is I’ve noticed I’m having trouble listening when people are talking to me. Like at the museum, someone will be telling me about the next art walk, and I’m looking right at them, but then I realize I missed the middle of what they said. I end up having to ask them to repeat it.
Have you noticed this kind of trouble focusing on conversations for as long as you can remember, or did it start more recently?

It’s been around a long time, I think. Even back in grade school my report cards would say things like “daydreams” or “needs reminders to finish work.” And before I was twelve, my mother would sit beside me when I did homework just to keep me on track.
When your mind drifts during conversations, are you often preoccupied with worries or anxious thoughts, or does your attention just wander without any particular worry on your mind?
I’m not totally sure. I don’t usually notice a specific worry running through my head when it happens. It’s more like I’m listening, and then my mind just kind of slips off somewhere else.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so, no. I haven’t really noticed feeling sad all the time or losing interest in things lately.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with chronic, longstanding inattentive symptoms (missing parts of conversations, mind wandering during listening) dating back to childhood, corroborated by school reports of 'daydreaming' and needing reminders to complete work, and requiring parental oversight for homework prior to age 12. These symptoms are not better explained by anxiety (no associated worry preoccupying attention) or depressive disorder (no anhedonia or persistent low mood reported). The clinical picture is most consistent with Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation.
